decision: transferred in faithful English; every printed/current difference is explicitly branched
source_reason: Both scans print the nilpotence-only alternative. It is an example offered for the already stated hypothesis that finite projective stalk modules are free. For A=k×k, J=rad(A)=0 is nilpotent, and P=k×0 is the image of the idempotent e(a,b)=(a,0). Tensoring along the two projections A→k gives dimensions(1,0) for P and(r,r) for A^r, so P is not free. The valid preceding residue-division-ring example remains: for a finite projective P over the stated A with D=A/J a division ring, lift a D-basis of P/JP to define f:A^r→P. Nakayama makes f surjective; projectivity splits A^r=P⊕K. Modulo J, D^r=(P/JP)⊕(K/JK) with the first summand already of dimension r, so K/JK=0. The finitely generated direct summand K is zero by Nakayama, hence f is an isomorphism. The cited Bourbaki II§3no.2, cor.2 of prop.5 keeps A/J a field as a standing assumption; finite presentation and nilpotence are its additional alternatives. Finite projectivity already gives finite presentation here. Delete the unsupported nilpotence disjunct from the example, without changing the lemma’s actual hypothesis. External source particulars are recorded in external_bourbaki_109.json.
